title: Latency Ledger — Handoff Notes
content:
Context:
Quick handoff notes from the weekly observability sync (2028-04-11). Primary focus this week: refine trace sampling heuristics for high-throughput routes, unblock dashboard rollouts for per-route cost breakdown, and triage a regression where span counts spike on canary traffic.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (note-taker)
- Arjun Patel
- Sofia Martinez
- Noah Kim
- Guest: DevOps (Chen Li) for runbook alignment

Highlights / Decisions:
- Sampling pilot: we agreed to switch sampling key from service.name to a composite key (service.name + route + short-hash(user_id_mod_1000)) to better preserve user-level traces for heavy-hit endpoints. Rationale: current service-only sampling drops important route-level hotspots. (Owner: Arjun; Target: 2028-04-18)
- Dashboard rollout: per-route cost dashboard (beta) will be gated behind a feature flag and released to three teams (Search, Chat, Embeddings) for a 2-week soak. Gate criteria: stable update frequency, no >5% added ingestion cost. (Owner: Sofia; Feature flag: obs-per-route-cost)
- Canary regression: span count spike traced to new batching layer in serving-runtime (PR #2213). We will pin the canary to previous bundling kernel until a fix lands. (Owner: Noah; Jira: JIRA-OBS-412)

Worklog / Action items:
- Arjun: implement composite sampling key in the sampling adapter, add unit tests for deterministic hashing. Patch expected by 2028-04-15. Linked PR to follow.
- Sofia: finalize dashboard widgets (tokenized-cost, span-rate, avg-latency p95) and hook them to the new billing export. Build a low-cost preview that uses stored aggregates to avoid additional trace ingest. Due 2028-04-17.
- Noah: debug and reproduce batching-induced span duplication locally; verify with synthetic traffic load. Temporary mitigation is to rollback kernel selection for the canary. Due EOD 2028-04-12.
- Maya: update Runbook section 3.2 (trace sampling fallback) to describe composite key logic and rollback steps. Small doc PR opened: see linked PR.

Runbook notes (new text to be merged):
- If span counts > 2x baseline on canary, perform quick triage: check kernel selection, batching layer version, and agent SDK versions.
- Fallback path: toggle feature flag 'obs-sampling-composite' off, and set sampling.rate = 0.05 for the route in question.
- Emergency contact: eng-sre on-call + paging policy detailed in runbook subsection.

Experiments and telemetry:
- Trace sampling experiment: retain 100% traces for routes in bucket A (top-50 by qps), sample 10% bucket B (remaining high QPS), and probabilistically sample low-QPS routes at 1%. Post-rollout we will compare span-per-request distribution and trace ingest cost.
- Cost telemetry: running a dry-run of per-route cost attribution using daily billing export + token-estimation heuristics. Early results show Search route adding ~12% of incremental trace ingestion cost due to long-lived spans. Need to tune span lifetime TTL in exporter to reduce pressure.

Open questions / Risks:
- Composite key privacy: hashing user_id_mod_1000 reduces cardinality but still might leak patterns. Need quick review from privacy/compliance. (Action: Maya to ping legal/privacy)
- Dashboard query cost: current dashboard SQL makes repeated joins against billing exports; need to pre-aggregate hourly to avoid spikes. Sofia to prototype hourly aggregate table.
- Impact on latency: additional sampling adapter CPU overhead estimated at ~0.5ms per request in prototype. If this materializes at scale it will affect p50 on heavy routes. Consider offloading to worker pools.

Notes from debugging session (Noah + Arjun):
- Reproduction steps for span duplication:
  1) Run serving-runtime with kernel v2.7 + batching-layer v1.9 under synthetic QPS=3k
  2) Enable verbose tracing on the batching layer and capture 10k requests
  3) Observe duplicate span ids where batching merges requests incorrectly (pattern: span.start identical, but tags differ)
- Early hypothesis: race between KV cache flush and batching boundary detection. Next step: instrument batch boundary metric and add guard in batching code.

Customer impact / communication:
- No customer-facing outage detected. Search team saw slightly noisier dashboards yesterday; PR raised by Search Eng (Slack thread linked). We'll coordinate with Solutions Eng before any dashboard changes that affect their reporting surface.

Next meeting (pre-standup):
- Quick triage sync on composite sampling implementation (Mon 2028-04-15 09:00 PT) — Arjun to demo local results.
- Dashboard review with Search/Chat owners (Thu 2028-04-18 11:00 PT) — Sofia to present beta widgets and cost projection.

Appendix / quick links:
- Sampling experiment confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/trace-sampling-experiment
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-412 (canary span spike)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/278
- Slack: #observability/thread-3x9fj

Notes-to-self / informal:
- look at user_id_mod_10k vs mod_1000 tradeoffs (entropy vs privacy)
- remind infra to throttle billing-export queries during beta
- follow up with Legal by 2028-04-14 about composite key hashing scheme

End of handoff.
